title: What HVAC techs do
d: HVAC technicians install and service heating, ventilation, and air conditioning: furnaces, heat pumps, AC condensers, ductwork, and controls. It blends mechanic
description: HVAC technicians install and service heating, ventilation, and air conditioning: furnaces, heat pumps, AC condensers, ductwork, and controls. It blends mechanical, electrical, and refrigeration skills, and EPA certification is legally required for handling refrigerants.

title: Essential tools
d: Manifold gauge set, vacuum pump, refrigerant scale, leak detector, multimeter, clamp meter, thermometers, tubing cutter and flaring tools, nitrogen regulator, a
description: Manifold gauge set, vacuum pump, refrigerant scale, leak detector, multimeter, clamp meter, thermometers, tubing cutter and flaring tools, nitrogen regulator, and a good drill set. Pros add: combustion analyzer, duct blaster, and recovery machine.

title: Key skills
d: Refrigeration cycle diagnostics (superheat/subcooling), electrical troubleshooting, brazing copper line sets, airflow measurement and duct design, combustion an
description: Refrigeration cycle diagnostics (superheat/subcooling), electrical troubleshooting, brazing copper line sets, airflow measurement and duct design, combustion analysis on furnaces, and reading wiring diagrams. Diagnostics separates techs: gauges tell a story if you can read it.

title: Safety essentials
d: Refrigerant displaces oxygen and can cause frostbite — ventilate and wear gloves. High voltage and capacitors: discharge before touching. Brazing needs fire wat
description: Refrigerant displaces oxygen and can cause frostbite — ventilate and wear gloves. High voltage and capacitors: discharge before touching. Brazing needs fire watch. Ladders and attics: heat exhaustion is the silent killer in summer.

title: Getting started
d: Trade school or apprenticeship, then EPA Section 608 certification (legally required). NATE certification boosts pay. Start in residential install or maintenanc
description: Trade school or apprenticeship, then EPA Section 608 certification (legally required). NATE certification boosts pay. Start in residential install or maintenance, specialize later in commercial or controls.

title: Pro tips
d: Check the simple things first: filters, breakers, thermostats, disconnects. Document superheat/subcooling on every call. Keep condensers clean — most no-cooling
description: Check the simple things first: filters, breakers, thermostats, disconnects. Document superheat/subcooling on every call. Keep condensers clean — most no-cooling calls are airflow. Sell maintenance agreements; they are recurring revenue.
